keyFindings.description: whenSent answers from the pending report taken before the re-mark: pending-sync counts a local update only after its IndexedDB write and an async report(), so on a document with nothing pending the wait resolves at once and the retry races the mark to the server; after an offline period with the socket still reconnecting, the retry is refused again and the reader sees the original 'anchor mark is not in the document'. Also: pendingRef is never reset on document change, the boolean is unread, and a real wait opens a window in which the auto-retry sends a draft older than the composer's (KEEP_DRAFT_MS debounce) and the landed send then clears the composer.

A selection across two blocks never re-anchors: placementOf returns null, readingsInBlock never finds a quote containing the block separator, so remarkRange always answers 'gone' and the reader is told the text was changed or deleted while it is on the page. Reproduced with a throwaway bun test ("two.\nBeta", mark dropped, state rebuilt -> {refused: 'gone'}). The NO_SURROUNDINGS comment and the test at record-mark-retype.test.ts:684 claim this case is handled.

The tracking plugin can never answer in production: y-prosemirror 1.3.7 applies every remote update as one tr.replace(0, size) (sync-plugin.js:629), which collapses every tracked range, and every local removal goes through removeRecordMark, which ends the entry. Its only test removes the mark with a local tr.removeMark. Delete it and restore removeRecordMark's contract.

The TTL is counted from the last sweep that saw the author, not from the author's last presence, so a socket drop just before the re-armed sweep removes the mark at once; README:2290, AGENTS.md:627-631, the changelog fragment and the PR body all claim 'counted from its author's last presence'.

'unplaceable' ('no longer where you selected it') is answered when two readings inside the reader's own block both match the surroundings, where the words are exactly where selected; margin-context.tsx:273 answers 'gone' ('changed or deleted') when the compose's document is merely not on screen. Both break the architect's 21:48Z rule that each refusal says a true thing.
